original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: Prove the all-n restored-source connectivity lower bound X >= 2(n-k), Q >= n+k for k historical source-interaction components; close PR1898's explicit source-XOR optimality question at Q=n+1, give the sharp projected Q/X frontier, and derive a sufficient global unequal-price optimality cone with unrestricted readouts.
scope_change_reason: The one added operation family is the paid elementary source XOR already established by PR1340. Rather than invent a duplicate extension or enlarge a finite census, follow PR1898's explicit missing all-word source-restoration lower bound. The permission for arbitrary readout multiplicities is inherited from PR1898, not from PR1370's paired-readout slice.
bottleneck_link: Temporary source mixing can replace expensive common-map calls; charging its unavoidable restoration prevents unsupported favorable recursive-interface budgets. This is a local tariff theorem, not an admitted supplier gain.
stop_rule: Prove or falsify the support-component potential before expanding evidence. Bound finite controls to GL(n,2), n<=4; dirty witnesses n<=8 and small dense maps. No broader mechanism or global unequal-price claim if this potential fails.
evidence: README all-n support-component and component-rank proof; RESULT exact 242940 GL transitions, bounded closed-word census, 66 partition witnesses, complete noncommuting dirty expansion/inverse, tariff724 and next-query floor738, 12 semantic controls; DENSE independently checks288 forward/inverse cases and5 controls. Focused package controls and CPython3.12 registered replay are the declared final checks.
author: Adam Gall
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) assistance in research, proof, implementation, experiments, and writing. No independent human or formal-kernel review is claimed.

optimistic_full_budget.model: Uniform complete Q/R/X prices b,a,x>0; every primitive includes arithmetic, coefficient and data access, private scratch, entry/exit frames, head return and dispatch. Add admission/preparation and any residual program-construction/storage bill separately.
optimistic_full_budget.new_proved_price_consequence: For n>=2 and Delta=(n+1)2^(n-1)-2(2^n-1), b>=Delta*a+2x suffices for the minimum-query word to be globally tariff-optimal. This is not the exact price-region boundary.
optimistic_full_budget.target: Prove no smaller X bill is possible at minimum Q, not report a new numerical saving. For intermediate Q, prove only the projected Q/X frontier and charge actual emitted readouts.
optimistic_full_budget.falsification: Any restored generic word with full-span queries and Q+X/2<2n, or any single CNOT changing the support-component count by more than one, refutes the proposed proof.

overlap.method: Shared snapshot consumed with --offline, local READMEs/TASK/merged review ledger, targeted live discussion1579 and1163/1166/1167.
overlap.limits: Offline data can miss subsequent changes; arbitrary code diffs and all closed work are not indexed. No match is not proof of novelty.
overlap.nearest: PR1898 explicitly leaves X optimality open; PR1370 fixes ten Q and62 R; PR1524 fixes equal Q/R prices. Neither supplies the all-n connectivity potential.

open_questions.question: What are the minimum total readouts on each intermediate Q/X frontier face?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Projected Q/X optimality does not determine the global tariff when readouts have positive price.
open_questions.first_step: At n=5 and Q=7, classify closed full-span prefix sets realizable at X=6 and compare their minimum even-subset readout sum.
open_questions.blocked_by: The connectivity theorem discards prefix geometry and cannot by itself prove a readout optimum.

open_questions.question: Does a selected supplier expose a legally mutable common-B boundary with favorable complete prices?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only an admitted caller can convert an abstract tariff result into a paid recursive gain.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an exact common map and exclusive source ownership, then price every source mutation, restoration, frame, routing, precision and program-storage obligation.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such physical caller or complete physical tariff is established here.
